name: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect with pulmonary stenosis
aliases: DORV with subaortic VSD and pulmonary stenosis
Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed VSD and pulmonary stenosis

criteria.description: Anatomic confirmation of both great arteries arising predominantly from the right ventricle
Presence of a subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect
Evidence of pulmonary stenosis causing obstruction to right ventricular outflow
Echocardiographic visualization of the abnormal ventricular-arterial connections and VSD
Cardiac MRI confirming anatomy and severity of pulmonary stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Anatomic confirmation of double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed VSD and presence of pulmonary stenosis by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography and cardiac MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis often present in neonatal period
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

pathognomonic.notes: Harsh ejection systolic murmur heard best at left upper sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur from narrowed pulmonary valve
systolic murmur due to pulmonary stenosis

common.notes: Reduced exercise capacity in infants and children
Rapid breathing due to cardiac insufficiency

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: liver swelling due to right heart problems

occasional.notes: Lower limb swelling in advanced cases
Transient loss of consciousness due to hypoxia or arrhythmia

searchTerms: stroke from embolism crossing heart defect
brain infarct due to embolus crossing circulation

rare.notes: Infective endocarditis on abnormal valves or septal defect

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Cardiac MRI confirming ventricular septal defect location and pulmonary stenosis
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and decreased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Overriding aorta rather than both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Typical four features including pulmonary stenosis, VSD, right ventricular hypertrophy, and overriding aorta
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
Absence of VSD or different VSD location
No pulmonary stenosis in classic form

references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomy and diagnosis. Heart. 2014;100(4):298-305.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital heart disease in infants and children. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2017;64(3):489-507.
Orphanet: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect with pulmonary stenosis (ORPHA:99043)
